topic: AI Search Visibility and Answer Engine Optimization
headline: Google Puts A Number On AI Search Clicks, Without The Data via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern
keyNotes: Google says its new AI features in search are already sending billions of clicks to websites every week, which is a lot, especially since they also say their regular search sends billions of clicks daily.

Even though Google is talking about billions of clicks, the special reports they give to website owners (called "Search Console") only show how many times their content was *seen* (impressions), not how many times people *clicked* on it from AI.
The big numbers Google shares are for *all* websites combined, so they don't tell individual website owners anything specific about how many people are clicking on *their* site because of AI.

Google hasn't shared the detailed information or how they calculated these "billions of clicks" numbers, which means website owners can't really check or compare them to their own website's performance.
question: If you were running a business and someone told you a new feature was sending "billions of clicks" to all businesses, but couldn't tell you how many clicks *your* business was getting, how would you decide if that feature was actually helping you?
